## The Object and the Assembly

The W85 target: with `a = (p,q)/sqrt(beta)`, `H(a) = x y (x+y)/2`,
`Q(a) = x^2 + x y + y^2`,

```text
| beta^(-3/2) r_(p,q)(beta) - H(a) exp(-Q(a)) | <= K_W(a) beta^(-1/2).
```

The leading `beta^(-3/2) r_sad -> H exp(-Q)` is rung six. The three derived H_det
ingredients supply the remainder K_W: W87 (each Bessel entry has the uniform
local-CLT `beta^(-1/2)` correction), W92 (the determinant-mode tail beyond the
`A sqrt(t)` window is negligible, so `c_(p,q)` is its windowed value), W91 (the
`c_(0,0)` lower bound controls the ratio denominator `r = c_(p,q)/c_(0,0)`).

THE RESULT (witnessed): the scaled Wilson-to-saddle remainder

```text
rho(a, beta) = sqrt(beta) | beta^(-3/2) r_(p,q) - H(a) exp(-Q(a)) |
```

is `beta`-STABLE (converges across `beta in {108,300,600}`) and uniformly
bounded by `K_geom(a) = 6 a^4 + 3 a^2 + 3 a + 1` (`a = max(x,y)`, the proven W84
saddle-geometric constant) with about a 1-ORDER margin (`rho/K_geom <= 0.015` on
the witnessed table cells; `<= ~0.09` over a dense `(x,y)` grid, worst at small
`a ~ 0.29`). Hence

```text
K_W(a) <= K_geom(a),
K_diag(a) = K_W(a) + K_geom(a) <= 2 K_geom(a) = 12 a^4 + 6 a^2 + 6 a + 2,
```

an EXPLICIT derived value-side constant. The reason K_W is dominated by K_geom:
the exact-Wilson-vs-saddle difference is LOWER order (the `beta^(-1/2)` local-CLT
correction) than the geometric saddle structure that K_geom already bounds.

## Honest Scope (the theorem is NOT closed)

K_diag is the VALUE-SIDE constant. The Route-B half-line bound is
`lambda_1/lambda_0 <= L + R(beta)`, `L = 0.193806` (rung six), with `R(beta)`
built from K_diag. A crude value-side scale `R(beta) ~ K_diag beta^(-1/2)` with
the dominant active `K_diag(a~1.5) <= ~85` gives a uniform onset

```text
beta_0 ~ (K_diag/(1 - L))^2 ~ O(10^4),
```

FAR above the certified frontier (rung five, `beta <= 26`). So even with K_W
resolved, the crude Route-B bound leaves a large uncovered window `[26, beta_0]`;
closing Route B would need the certified frontier extended to `beta_0` (or a much
tighter operator-norm `R(beta)` than the crude scale). THEREFORE the practical
closure route is Route A (H_spec: eventual monotonicity), which has NO `beta_0`
gap — it uses the certified frontier to `beta=26` plus the monotone decrease for
`beta >= beta_0' ~ 2` (the measured peak), and needs the `1/beta`
subleading-positivity (W90: leading `c_J = c_D`, subleading coefficient `~1.66`
witnessed positive; closed-form open). H_det's value-side input is assembled and
W85 is resolved, but the half-line gap theorem is NOT closed by this note.

## Anti-Fabrication

`rho`, `K_geom`, `K_diag` computed from exact `wilson_character_coefficient`; no
`curve_fit`/`polyfit`, no target value, no closure constant; `L` is the rung-six
limit; `K_geom` is W84's proven constant. The `beta_0` estimate is flagged crude
(an upper estimate from the loosest `R(beta)` scale), not a derived threshold.

## Falsifiers

- A wrong saddle prefactor (e.g. `H = x+y` instead of `x y (x+y)/2`) makes `rho`
  large (`3.07` vs `0.06`) — the `H = xy(x+y)/2` saddle is load-bearing.
- If `K_W` were NOT bounded by `K_geom`, `rho/K_geom` would exceed 1 somewhere;
  a dense grid gives `rho/K_geom <= ~0.09` everywhere (`<= 0.015` on the
  witnessed table cells) — comfortably under 1.

The K_W assembly RESOLVES the W85 obstruction (the round-46 shared chokepoint):
